text: SLICE 6 ADDED - codec, and the reason it was MISSING is a flaw in the chief's scoping, not an oversight of scale. CheckedSidecarPrelude (sidecar.scala:329), CheckedSidecarBlock (sidecar.scala:341), SidecarBlockRange (sidecar.scala:221). All three are case classes with private[codec] constructors and therefore public fromProduct; the two Checked types are minted only by 'new Checked...' behind the verifying gate at sidecar.scala:537 and :573. Their Scaladoc states the guarantee fromProduct breaks: the prelude is 'verified against evidence that did not come from the sidecar file itself', and the block exists so that 'a partial fetch must never masquerade as validation of the complete sidecar'. Forging either mints a witness that witnessed nothing. THEY WERE ABSENT FROM THE ORIGINAL SLICE PLAN because they never entered the 45-item validating list, because they have no self-validating companion - the same heuristic flaw that mis-ranked AuthorizedRemoteRequest. It did not merely misorder work; it deleted a module from the plan. ADOPTED RANKING RULE, superseding the earlier one: A TYPE WHOSE NAME IS AN ASSERTION IS THE WORST TO LEAVE FORGEABLE - Checked-, Authorized-, Validated-, -Receipt, -Proof, -Witness. Such types exist only to carry a claim that verification happened, and they are exactly the ones a self-validation search cannot see because their verification is by construction elsewhere. Read the Scaladoc, not just the signature: the grep says what a type IS, the doc says what it PROMISES, and the promise determines what a forged instance costs. STILL TO CHECK under this rule: align StructuralReductionReceipt (cost.scala:175, built by wire.scala) and the remaining externally-gated types.
